title: Check sorted weights instead of original sample weights during percentile averaging
answers: Why does _weighted_percentile return NaN at percentile rank 100 when average=True?
How should zero-weight neighbors be detected in _weighted_percentile with NaNs?
Fix _weighted_percentile returning NaN on inputs with missing values and average=True
body:
Symptom: Calling _weighted_percentile on arrays containing NaNs with average=True produces NaN at percentile_rank=100 instead of ignoring NaNs.
Root cause: sklearn/utils/stats.py:_weighted_percentile indexed into the original sample_weight instead of sorted_weights when checking if the next rank had zero weight, bypassing zeroed-out NaN weights.
Fix pattern: Check zero-weight adjacent positions against sorted_weights using sorted indices (percentile_plus_one_indices) rather than indexing original sample_weight.
Constraints: Applies when weights are reordered or modified (such as zeroing weights for NaNs) prior to computing CDF lookahead; does not apply when weights remain unsorted or unmodified.
applies: sklearn/utils/stats.py:_weighted_percentile when computing weighted percentiles with average=True on data with NaNs
